name: Oxymetholone

card.summary: Anadrol: an anemia drug that bodybuilders use as a potent oral bulker, with a well-documented liver-toxicity profile and almost no physique trials.
card.note: 17-alpha-alkylated oral steroid; hepatotoxicity (peliosis hepatis, liver tumours) is documented in medical use.

quick.overview:
Oxymetholone, sold as Anadrol, is an oral anabolic-androgenic steroid approved in some countries for anemias caused by bone-marrow failure. In bodybuilding and looksmaxxing forums it is discussed as a strong oral for mass and fullness, and some users pair it with injectable testosterone in cycles.

The published research is about its medical use, not its effect on appearance. Hematology reviews describe it, with danazol, as one of the androgens commonly used in inherited marrow failure, and a general-purpose reference text describes lean-mass gains in short-term wasting studies.
quick.mechanism: It is a 17-alpha-alkylated derivative of dihydrotestosterone that activates the androgen receptor and also stimulates red-cell production. The alkylation permits oral use but is associated with liver stress.[1][2]
quick.risks: Reviews of androgen therapy for marrow failure report virilization and liver toxicity as major adverse events, and case series link oral androgens to peliosis hepatis and liver tumours.[2][3][4] Forum users also discuss unfavourable cholesterol effects and gynecomastia.[5][6] It is a controlled substance in many places and banned in sport.

lead: Oxymetholone (brand names include Anadrol and Anapolon) is a synthetic oral anabolic-androgenic steroid derived from dihydrotestosterone. It is a 17-alpha-alkylated compound, a structural change that allows oral dosing and that is associated with hepatic toxicity.[1] Its medical role has been in anemias due to deficient red-cell production, such as aplastic anemia and Fanconi anemia.[2][7]

In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding communities, oxymetholone is mentioned as a potent oral for rapid mass and a full look, often discussed alongside other orals such as methandienone, stanozolol and superdrol, and sometimes in teen or young-adult cycle threads.[8][9][10][11] T Nation posters describe it both as harsh on blood lipids and liver and as having a reputation that is, in their view, heavier than warranted at lower doses.[5][12]

No published trial located has tested oxymetholone for cosmetic or physique goals in healthy people. The clinical studies that exist concern anemias and related uses and report benefit in a subset of patients alongside virilization and liver toxicity.[2][7][13]

paras: Oxymetholone has been used as an androgen therapy for bone-marrow failure. A hematology review states that androgens are the main non-transplant therapy for marrow failure in dyskeratosis congenita and Fanconi anemia, reporting responses in up to 80 percent of cases, with danazol and oxymetholone the most commonly used and virilization and liver toxicity the major adverse events.[2] A review of androgen therapy in aplastic anaemia noted that earlier reports of response rates comparable to marrow transplantation had given way to markedly lower recovery rates in later reports, possibly reflecting differences in supportive care and in evaluation of residual marrow function.[7] Small clinical studies of oxymetholone in bone-marrow insufficiency date to the 1970s.[14]

Androgens including oxymetholone were also tested for anemia in dialysis patients, and a Cochrane review examined androgen therapy for the anemia of chronic kidney disease in adults.[13][15] A controlled trial found that nandrolone decanoate and oxymetholone did not protect the bone marrow from suppression during methotrexate chemotherapy.[16] Grokipedia, an AI-generated encyclopedia, also describes experimental use for HIV-associated wasting and heart failure; these claims are not sourced here to primary trials.[1]

Users on looksmaxxing forums consider oxymetholone for muscle mass and for a masculinised physique and face. A post from a user in Argentina asked whether oxymetholone or stanozolol would be more useful to masculinise the face and physique, and others asked which oral to add to a stack for mass.[9][10] Another thread asks which SERM to pair with oxymetholone, and a teenager's posted cycle plan describes adding oxymetholone to a testosterone-based stack alongside other compounds.[17][8] These are user reports; no controlled trial has assessed such outcomes.

Clinical studies of oxymetholone concern anemias, not appearance: a 1974 trial in bone-marrow insufficiency, a controlled trial showing no protection of marrow during methotrexate chemotherapy, a randomized comparison of androgens for anemia in hemodialysis patients, and a Cochrane review of androgens for anemia of chronic kidney disease (eight studies, 181 participants).[14][16][13][15] No trial has tested it for physique or facial outcomes in healthy people.

The medical literature on androgen therapy identifies virilization and liver toxicity as major adverse events.[2] A review of androgens and liver tumours reported that the association between anabolic androgenic steroids and hepatic tumours was first noted in patients with Fanconi anemia, and examined whether non-Fanconi patients and those given parenteral androgens are also at risk.[4] A series of twelve cases of peliosis hepatis was reported in association with oral androgen therapy.[3] The U.S. Report on Carcinogens includes a profile of oxymetholone.[18]

A review of supraphysiologic-dose anabolic-androgenic steroid use proposed that it may be a risk factor for dementia, based on parallels with Alzheimer-type brain abnormalities and on mechanisms involving androgen disturbance and oxidative stress; it addresses AAS generally rather than oxymetholone specifically.[19] A rat study of four anabolic steroids, including oxymetholone, found increased dopaminergic and serotonergic activity in brain regions after long-term treatment.[20]

T Nation contributors note that orals such as oxymetholone depress HDL cholesterol and raise LDL more than injectables, that gynecomastia can occur early, and that oxymetholone has been called harsh, though one poster argued that dose is the relevant factor.[5][12][6] A thread on kidney effects also circulated binding-affinity data for oxymetholone.[21]

Grokipedia describes oxymetholone as an androgen-receptor agonist that also stimulates erythropoiesis, possibly via erythropoietin and effects on marrow progenitors.[1] Relative-binding studies of anabolic steroids found that some compounds, among them oxymetholone, bound the androgen receptor too weakly to measure, a point noted in forum discussions of how it acts.[21][22]

On T Nation, users discuss oxymetholone as a medically indicated drug for anemias and wasting that is not appropriate to take for bodybuilding, and as one of the substances on lists of prohibited anabolic agents for natural contests.[23][24] Forum threads treat it as part of oral stacks, and members debate low-dose versus higher-dose approaches.[25][12]

lore.intro: Oxymetholone is discussed on looksmaxxing and bodybuilding forums as a strong oral for mass; users trade cycle plans while others warn about cholesterol and liver effects.[8][10][5]

claims.claim: Anadrol is a powerful oral for fast mass and fullness.
claims.believers: Forum users list it with other orals as an option to add to a stack to escape a skinny-fat look.[10][11]
claims.experts: The published trials concern anemia and wasting; none has measured physique outcomes in healthy people.[2][13]

claims.claim: Anadrol can masculinise the face and body.
claims.believers: A forum poster asked whether it would be more useful than stanozolol for masculinising face and physique.[9]
claims.experts: No published study has examined facial or aesthetic effects of oxymetholone; clinical reviews report virilization as an adverse effect in patients.[2]

claims.claim: Its reputation for harshness is overstated at low doses.
claims.believers: One T Nation poster argued the drug's reputation depends on dose and that results can be obtained at lower amounts.[25][12]
claims.experts: Reviews list liver toxicity as a major adverse event, and case series link oral androgens with peliosis hepatis and liver tumours.[2][3][4]

claims.claim: Orals like oxymetholone damage cholesterol far more than injectables.
claims.believers: T Nation posters state that it crushes HDL and raises LDL more than injectable compounds.[5]
claims.experts: No dedicated published lipid trial of oxymetholone was located; forum posters cite general literature on androgen-induced dyslipidemia.[26]
